## What the data says
- All eight nearest thin-fabric test runs at 20.7-21.6 % O₂ and 101.3 kPa sustained burning; distance-weighted share = 100 % [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric at ISS conditions is 0.986 (scale 0-1) [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Physics estimate (n-heptane surrogate) gives an adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2270 K, about 50 K below the hottest thin-fabric microgravity test (≈ 2320 K) and about 260 K above the coldest burning test (≈ 2010 K) [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Thin solid (films, sheets) runs: 7 sustained, 1 marginal; distance-weighted share ≈ 93.8 % [PSI-25]
- Evidence coverage for thin solid is 1.0 [PSI-25]
- Physics estimate for thin solid places the adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2270 K, ≈ 50 K below the hottest thin-solid test (≈ 2330 K) and ≈ 360 K above the coldest burning test (≈ 1910 K) [PSI-25]
- Fire-resistant materials (Nomex, silicone) had 3 of 4 Nomex runs burn and 1 not; 0 of 4 silicone runs burned (total 3/8 burned) [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 showed Nomex HT90-40 failed at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g (NTRS 20070018178)
- Partial-gravity data are absent; NASA FM2 researchers note oxygen needed for flame spread may be lowest near lunar gravity, so partial gravity could be more hazardous than both micro- and Earth-gravity (NTRS 20260000646)

## How confident we can be
- Confidence for thin fabric derives from evidence coverage 0.986; almost all solid runs are "sustained," so a flammability limit cannot be located (131 of 134 solid runs sustained) [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99]
- Confidence for thin solid is maximal (coverage = 1.0) but limited by the same lack of non-burning runs (see solid data limitation) [PSI-25]
- Fire-resistant material confidence is low; only eight runs exist, with mixed outcomes, and no predictor estimate is provided [PSI-25] [PSI-99]

## Gaps
- No microgravity test data for thin fabric at oxygen levels above 22.2 % or at pressures different from ~101 kPa
- No partial-gravity combustion data; lunar or Martian gravity effects are untested and may be more hazardous (NTRS 20260000646)
- Solid data lack sufficient extinction points to define a flammability limit for any solid class (131/134 sustained) [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99]
- Fire-resistant materials were not tested at higher oxygen concentrations; predictor gives no estimate for them

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric burning at oxygen concentrations > 22 % and at varied pressures to locate a flammability limit
- Partial-gravity flame spread for thin fabrics and thin solids to assess hazard in lunar and Martian gravity (FM2)
- Additional solid runs that intentionally achieve extinction (lower flow, lower O₂) to establish true limits for thin solids and films
- Fire-resistant material tests at higher O₂ (up to 30 %) and in partial gravity to verify behavior beyond current microgravity runs
- Droplet combustion of surrogate fuels on thin fabrics to compare solid vs. liquid fire behavior under identical atmospheres.
